cited_evidence: Exact handoff evidence shows evidence_sources producer_sha256 and consumer_sha256 are identical: sha256:8a65517fc4985942cb1867d67ab450ff9cc4a1de9cb9abf11cff7745c371e17a.
Job 2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08 while needs/coverage record_id values are n06-r01 through n06-r08.

Upstream assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_weight': record.get('source_weight', 0), 'rank': index}, replacing the demand record identity with the source identity.
Job 2 prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources.record_id and then looks up coverage.get('record_id'), so mismatched identities cause all observed priorities to have upstream_rank: 0.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution contains a fault in the upstream provenance assembly. Job 2 received exact handoffs, so the downstream job consumed the upstream evidence as produced. The upstream assemble_provenance function writes evidence_sources.record_id from source_id instead of preserving the need record_id, producing records like s01/s02 rather than n06-r01/n06-r02. Job 2 then cannot join provenance ranks to coverage record_ids, yielding upstream_rank 0 for every priority and violating the requirement to preserve upstream provenance order/ranks.
